battery.prompt: At a community repair cafe, you and three unfamiliar volunteers have twenty minutes before visitors arrive. The tools are already laid out, nobody has assigned roles, and there is no urgent problem. Describe what you actually do first and write the first two sentences you say, if any.

A friend wants to turn your planned quiet walk into a crowded street festival. You would mildly prefer the walk, but either option is possible and nobody is relying on you. Write your actual reply and choose what you do next.

You find an unfamiliar brass object in a secondhand shop. It is affordable, has no label, and the seller does not know what it does. You have fifteen spare minutes. Choose what you do, describe the first action, and say what attracts or discourages you.

You have forty minutes free and a small unfinished creative project on your desk. Finishing it today is optional. Several new ideas also interest you. Describe how you actually spend the forty minutes and what will remain on the desk afterward.

A friend sends only: "That conversation stayed with me." You do not know whether they mean this positively or negatively, and there was no argument. Write your reply and describe what you do during the next ten minutes.

Two friends disagree about the ending of a film: one calls it hopeful, the other calls it dishonest. You found it unresolved. They ask for your view. Write what you actually say, then describe what you want to happen in the conversation.

You enter a nearly empty gallery with one unfamiliar abstract sculpture and a bench. You have ten minutes and no obligation to stay. Describe what you actually do and the thoughts that guide that choice.
